findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading, roll call 758 (passed 66 to 47)
findings.note: Voted aye on second reading of an omnibus election bill. Per the legislature's staff analysis (https://dashboard.ncleg.gov/api/Services/BillSummary/2025/H958-SMST-37(rat)-v-8), its voter-registration part would have the DMV send full Social Security numbers to the elections board monthly, create a process to remove registered voters who a federal database shows are not citizens, and bar processing any registration that does not affirmatively say the applicant is a citizen (with a sworn form sent to applicants who left it blank). He is not a listed sponsor.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House concurrence in Senate changes), roll call 801 (passed 62 to 47)
findings.note: Voted aye on the final House concurrence vote on the same omnibus election bill (citizenship statement on registration, removal of non-citizens from voter rolls, fewer early-voting days, post-election audits). The bill was ratified August 6, 2026 and vetoed by the Governor August 17, 2026; per the staff analysis it is not current law unless the veto is overridden.

findings.motion: HB 834 State Board of Elections Administrative Changes, M11 Concur, roll call 800 (passed 74 to 35)
findings.note: Voted aye on House concurrence for the bill that became S.L. 2026-60. Per the legislature's staff analysis (https://dashboard.ncleg.gov/api/Services/BillSummary/2025/H834-SMBK-32(sl)-v-8), it requires an eligibility affidavit when a relative or guardian hand-delivers a voter's mail-in absentee ballot, sets a deadline for curing ballot deficiencies, directs county boards to decide whether to count a provisional ballot when the no-photo-ID affidavit is found likely false, and treats a driver license in a two-year extension as valid photo ID for voting through December 31, 2027. He is not a listed sponsor.
